about: Sarcastic Bear shows a young brown bear sitting upright among mossy rocks and grass, head tipped back, eyes rolled up and mouth hanging open in what looks exactly like a theatrical "oh, wow, really?" The expression reads as mock surprise or exaggerated apology, so captions put dripping sarcasm in its mouth. It's the animal version of a person answering an obvious question with fake astonishment, in the same family as Condescending Wonka.
origin: A Redditor posted the photo to r/funny in May 2014 with a title noting how sarcastic the bear looked, and it was soon captioned as an advice-animal image.
usage:
The top box is usually a mock-sincere opener ("oh I'm so sorry", "wow, really?") and the bottom box finishes the sarcastic reply. Treat it as the bear responding to someone who asked something obvious, complained unreasonably, or expected you to know something nobody could.

It suits customer service frustrations, coworkers asking questions answered in the email, gamers blaming lag, and friends acting shocked at the predictable. The more over-the-top the faux politeness, the better the open-mouthed face matches it.
